slides.title: Property transfer tax
slides.subtitle: The closing cost nobody puts on their vision board

slides.title: A one-time tax when you buy
slides.body: BC charges property transfer tax when you buy a property registered at the Land Title Office. Separate from yearly property taxes. Yes, there are two.
1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, and 3% above $2 million. A further 2% applies to residential value over $3 million.

slides.title: A $700,000 home
slides.body: 1% of $200,000 = $2,000. 2% of the next $500,000 = $10,000. Total: $12,000. Better to meet that number here than at the lawyer's office.

slides.title: Up to $8,000 off
slides.body: Eligible first-time buyers pay none on homes worth $500,000 or less, and get $8,000 off up to $835,000. It phases out by $860,000.

slides.title: $12,000 becomes $4,000
slides.body: For an eligible first-time buyer, the $8,000 exemption brings the tax on a $700,000 home down to $4,000. That's a lot of patio furniture.

slides.title: The fine print
slides.body: Canadian citizen or permanent resident, lived in BC for a year (or filed 2 BC tax returns in the last 6 years), and never owned a principal residence anywhere.

slides.title: Move in and stay
slides.body: Move in within 92 days, and live there as your principal residence until the first anniversary of registration. It's a commitment.

slides.title: Brand new home?
slides.body: The newly built home exemption covers new homes up to $1.1 million, with a partial exemption up to $1.15 million. Its rules differ.

slides.title: Planning your first purchase?
slides.body: I can set you up with an appointment with a qualified mortgage professional to map out the full cost.

caption:
Property transfer tax in BC, explained for first-time home buyers 🧾 (aka the closing cost nobody brags about on Instagram)

When you buy a home in BC, you pay a one-time property transfer tax (separate from your yearly property taxes):
• 1% on the first $200,000
• 2% from $200,000 to $2 million
• 3% above $2 million (plus a further 2% on residential value over $3 million)

On a $700,000 home, that's $12,000.

First-time buyer? If you qualify, you pay no property transfer tax on a home worth $500,000 or less, and get an $8,000 exemption up to $835,000. It phases out between $835,000 and $860,000. On that $700,000 home, $12,000 becomes $4,000. That's a lot of patio furniture 🪑

The main rules: Canadian citizen or permanent resident, lived in BC for at least a year before registration (or filed 2 BC tax returns in the last 6 years), never owned a principal residence anywhere in the world, and never received this exemption before. You need to move in within 92 days and live there until the first anniversary of registration.

Buying a newly built home? There's a separate exemption with higher limits.

Your lawyer or notary applies the exemption when your purchase is registered, so ask them to confirm your situation. Want to plan the full cost of buying? I can set you up with an appointment with a qualified mortgage professional. Just send me a DM.

📌 Save this, and send it to the friend who keeps saying "next year" about buying.

sources.claim: PTT rates: 1% to $200K, 2% $200K–$2M, 3% over $2M, further 2% on residential value over $3M; applies when you purchase/gain an interest in property registered at the LTO
$700,000 example: $2,000 + $10,000 = $12,000 (arithmetic from official rates; matches the gov.bc.ca worked examples method)
FTHB exemption (registered on/after Apr 1, 2024): full to $500K; $8,000 over $500K to $835K; proportionally reduced over $835K and under $860K

Eligibility: citizen/PR; lived in BC 1 year before registration or filed 2 BC returns in last 6 years; never owned a principal residence anywhere; never received the exemption; move in within 92 days; occupy until first anniversary; legal professional applies it
Newly built home exemption: full to $1,100,000, partial under $1,150,000 (registered on/after Apr 1, 2024)
No announced changes to PTT rates or FTHB thresholds since (gov.bc.ca property tax updates list only purpose-built rental and admin changes in 2025–26)
